goal: Build an integrated pre-drill package. It needs an interval-segmented ROP regression for the FORGE Pason data (2-sigma anomalies, CV, 75th-percentile envelope) and BOEM OGOR-A 2024 decline parameters with a weighted top-15 intervention ranking. It also needs OU/OGS mud-log/core matching by API (with >50 ft flags and formation tops) and a risk matrix plus a personnel gap check. Deliver an Excel workbook and a technical memo with executive summary, data quality issues, recommendations with confidence levels, and a sources appendix.
delivered: output/ holds integrated_pre_drill_technical_package.xlsx (README, ROP_Model with 9 intervals, ROP_Anomalies, ROP_Envelope, Production_Decline, Intervention_Top15, OGS_Matches, Formation_Tops, Risk_Matrix, Personnel_Gaps, Data_Lineage) and technical_memo.docx. Both use real BOEM 2019-2024 and OU/OGS downloads.
what_went_wrong: Production decline was fitted as log-linear exponential (annual decline = 1 - exp(12 x slope)), so the Arps Di and b the rubric expects were never estimated. ROP envelopes were computed per interval (q75 from 9.54 to 389 ft/hr), not as one global 75th-percentile threshold. That global value is 44.3 ft/hr and easy to compute, and the prompt can be read either way. Memo recommendations carry High/Moderate labels with no stated R-squared or corroboration criteria. The API item failed because BOEM Gulf APIs were not truncated to a key shared with the Oklahoma OGS data, although those wells cannot overlap.

failed_items.why: The prompt says 'For each interval, perform multivariate regression ... then identify the operating envelope where ROP exceeds the 75th percentile'. The agent read this per interval and ROP_Envelope gives P10-P90 WOB/RPM/pump ranges per interval. The rubric expects a single global q75 of 44.3 ft/hr (it is 44.295 on drilling_data_processed.csv), a reading the prompt does not state.

README and memo: 'decline is log-linear on positive oil months'. Production_Decline has only oil_log_slope_per_month and annual_decline_rate, with no Di or b. The agent chose an exponential fit instead of the standard Arps hyperbolic and never mentions Arps in the trajectory.

The executive summary is quantified and the data-quality section exists. The recommendations table assigns High/Moderate, but the memo never defines confidence levels by R-squared bands or cross-source corroboration (judge).

Mud-log (10-digit) to core (14-digit) matching on the first 10 digits is done and documented. The criterion fails only because BOEM 12-digit Gulf APIs were not truncated to a key shared with the Oklahoma OGS wells, and those datasets cannot share wells. The drilling DB has named wells (WD-031-L013) and no APIs, so no conversion would have enabled a match, as the memo documents.

subagent_notes: Two background subagents ran at the start: one profiled the local CSV and DB schemas, the other researched public BOEM/OGS download URLs (6 tool errors from failed fetches). The root then downloaded the BOEM and OGS data itself. Both were helpful scouting and not linked to any failed item.
